whatItFakes: Each outcome the web keeps (crime, schooling, coverage, turnout and the rest) stays at its place's real starting level except where a researched link moves it; nothing else in the world moves it.
why: The research's drift sizes (data/research/outcome-web/place-outcome-bases-2024.json, defaultDrift) include a monthly chance of a society-wide wave, which the no-dice rule forbids; the causes behind drift are not yet modeled.
replacement: Each outcome moved by the engines that cause it (a crime engine, schools, health coverage, elections), with the web's factor on top, and society-wide shifts from recorded causes rather than a monthly chance.

whatItFakes: Full couples decide on a child from their own age, children, work, income, room, savings, health and closeness, and none of the outcome web's birth links reach them. Counted women take the web's factor per woman (src/core2/births-counted.ts), so a full woman and a counted woman of the same age, tenure and place differ on the links the full decision does not carry: home prices (owners up, renters down), an enforced abortion ban, and the place's drifting birth level.
why: The unemployment link is left out for full couples on purpose: a lost job already lowers their work and income terms, so the web's link would count the same recession twice. The other links have no term in the plan score, and the score is a choice between planning and waiting, not a rate the factor can multiply; turning a factor into a score term needs its own calibration against the births it produces.
replacement: A conditions term in the plan score that reads webReach for the woman's own age and tenure, leaving out the links her own records already carry (unemployment), with a weight calibrated in a played year so full births move by the researched size, as counted births do.
resolution: Full couples' plan-a-child choice carries a web term in the plan score: renewalWebWeight times the birth-rate factor that lands on the mother's own age and home, less one (webFactorFor in src/core2/births-plan.ts), the same factor the counted women of that age and home are scaled by (src/core2/births-counted.ts). Unemployment, home prices and the abortion law now move full couples' plans, pregnancies and births as they move the counted tier's. The unemployment link is read through the factor like the others, so its effect is shared with the work and income terms. src/core2/births-full-web.test.ts follows a shifted web month row to the plans, pregnancies and births it tips in a played year, by record id.

whatItFakes: The town hears of a rise in housing.rent from the outcome web's month record, but no engine yet reads the web's rent factor when it sets a lease, so the rise the story reports is not in any lease or rent payment.
why: The housing family's rent wiring is on its own branch; the news path lists the measure so the town hears of it the month an engine reads it, with no change here.
replacement: The housing engine multiplies its lease rent by webFactorFor(housing.rent); then this row and the readBy null in data/news/outcome-news.json are replaced by the reading file.

whatItFakes: A full person's leaving does not weigh the state income tax in force: only counted households do (counted-moves.ts reads the town state's income-tax law and the other states' 2026 table into an income pull). The web's income-tax links are about zero (Young, Varner, Lurie and Prisinzano 2016), so they add nothing on top, and adding them would count the tax twice for counted households.
why: A full person's destination is chosen after the pull is built, so a tax difference between states has no place to enter the pull until a destination-aware pull exists.
replacement: A destination-aware pull for full people that uses the same net-of-tax income comparison as pullBetween in counted-moves.ts.

whatItFakes: The link from a severe disaster to out-migration (Boustan, Kahn, Rhode and Yanguas 2020) does not run: no record says how many people a disaster killed in a place. The disasters engine holds FEMA declarations (type, begin and declared dates) with no deaths, and the research's effect starts at about 100 deaths.
why: A declaration is not a severity; reading one as severe would move every declared place by a guess.
replacement: A per-place count of deaths from a disaster (the health engine's cause-of-death records within the incident's dates) read as the link's cause disaster.severe.
resolution: The link runs: the web reads disaster.severe from the disasters engine's news events (severeDisasterReading in src/core2/modules/disasters.ts) and the moves engines read its factor on population.out-migration (webLeavingFor). What stands in for deaths is registered as SG-WEB-disaster-severity-damage-proxy. Shown in src/core2/law-wiring-disasters-web.test.ts.

whatItFakes: Two housing links move nothing through the web: air-conditioning use does not rise or fall with the electricity price, and the share of income a place's renters pay in rent adds no factor to how many people are homeless. The housing engine's own evictions do follow unpaid rent (a named household's lease by its own pay and cash; counted households by their group's pooled arrears, lowest income first), but no played year yet shows that path rising with burden past 22 and faster past 32 percent.
why: The cited research gives no usable size: the electricity-price link has no published slope and no engine reads the air-conditioning share; the rent-burden link has thresholds at 22 and 32 percent but no slope (Zillow and UNH 2018; Colburn and Aldern 2022), and src/core2/housing-calibration.test.ts checks the curve only in a year with 10 or more court cases, which the drawn towns did not reach and the pinned Puerto Rico town fails.
replacement: A sized link (a published slope per cent of price) read by an engine that decides air-conditioning use; for rent burden, a played year with 10 or more court cases that passes the burden checks in src/core2/housing-calibration.test.ts, after which the link is carried by the housing engine.

whatItFakes: A severe disaster does not lower home values: the link needs the disaster's death toll and the disasters module records only the FEMA declaration and its payments.
why: Boustan, Kahn, Rhode and Yanguas 2020 size the price effect for disasters with at least 20 deaths; no record of deaths per disaster exists, and home values are not a factor the sales engine reads.
replacement: Deaths and damage recorded on each disaster by the disasters module, and the housing sales engine reading the web's home-price factor.
resolution: The link runs: the disasters module records a severity on each disaster's news event and the web reads it as disaster.severe; the housing engine values owned homes and prices purchases and sales at the web's factor on housing.home-value (ownedHomes, sellHome and the renters' purchase price in src/core2/modules/housing.ts). What stands in for deaths is registered as SG-WEB-disaster-severity-damage-proxy. Shown in src/core2/law-wiring-disasters-web.test.ts.

whatItFakes: A severe disaster (Boustan, Kahn, Rhode and Yanguas 2020: severe by deaths, about 25 or more in a county in a decade) is read from the homes FEMA inspected as damaged in the town per resident, not from deaths. The game's disasters kill no one, and FEMA declarations carry no deaths. The reading is a ramp from 0 at the 90th percentile of the game's own FEMA town rows (0.0526 damaged homes per resident) to 1 at the 95th (0.1157), the cutoffs Roth Tran and Wilson 2023 (FRBSF Working Paper 2020-34, p. 7 and p. 24) draw for damages per capita, ranked here over FEMA's town rows matched to a Census place by name (9,887 rows; 7,997 unmatched or ambiguous rows left out) rather than their SHELDUS county-months. The researched size of the three links that start from it (home values -5.2%, out-migration +5%, non-disaster transfers +2%) applies at a reading of 1 and in proportion below it; the study found no effect from milder disasters, and Roth Tran and Wilson find the average FEMA declaration leaves prices flat and then 1.4% higher. A disaster counts for the ten years after it begins (Boustan's decade). The effect applies from the start, though Roth Tran and Wilson find prices strongly higher one to three years after a very severe disaster and strongly lower only over the longer run. A disaster whose damage FEMA's figures do not show for the town (no row, or no recorded population) reads as no severity, though the damage is unknown. A disaster hits only the player's town (the one place the disasters engine keeps records of); other places read nothing.
why: No source sizes the effect of a FEMA declaration itself on prices or moving except Roth Tran and Wilson, who find none for the average declaration, so reading every declaration as severe would move every declared place by a guess; the study's deaths are not recorded, so damage stands in for them.
replacement: Deaths from a disaster recorded by the health engine's cause-of-death records within the incident's dates (SHELDUS-style county damages per capita if a source of them is added as data), read as disaster.severe; and a disasters engine that records damage to businesses, public buildings and people, so severity is not one town figure.
resolution: Resolved Oct 28: the outcome web reads disaster.severe from the disasters engine's news events (severity from the homes FEMA found damaged per resident, SG-WEB-disaster-severity-damage-proxy), and the housing engine values each home, and prices each purchase and sale, at the home-values link's factor (law-wiring-disasters-web.test.ts).

whatItFakes: The graduation-to-turnout link moves turnout from the web's own school.graduation-pct number, which is a ledger value that no school outcomes engine produces.
why: The school module keeps no graduation outcomes by place, so the cause is the web's baseline plus its own links (universal pre-K, tuition freeze), not students who graduated.
replacement: A school outcomes engine that records graduates by place and year; the link then reads that record, lagged five years.

whatItFakes: The newspaper-closure-to-engagement link into local turnout runs (the web counts the town's closed local newspapers from the press module, and the voting engine multiplies a voter's turnout propensity by its effect on a day with a local race), but its cause does not occur in play: no local newspaper closes, so the count stays at zero and the link moves no one.
why: A paper closes only by its owner's choice, which the business engine weighs from the paper's operating losses and the owner's age, and the press books each paper's shortfall to its wider audience every week (SG-PEOPLE-press-bureau-shortfall), so a paper's books show no losses; in four drawn places over 800 days none closed.
replacement: An outlet whose revenue from its own readers and advertisers falls short of its costs without the wider audience's weekly top-up, so its books show the operating losses the owner's closing decision weighs; the web then counts it closed with no change to the link.

whatItFakes: The exposed-corruption-to-reelection link into the incumbent's reelection is not run.
why: The voting engine already reads each reported scandal into the incumbent's appeal (scandalsOf), so a web factor on the reelection rate would move it twice; the cause is not a number the web can read.
replacement: Resolved Oct 24: the link is carried by the voting engine (carriedBy in links.json): scandalTerm and scandalAppeal in src/core2/modules/voting.ts lower a candidate's appeal with each voter a bribe or conviction story reached, so the web does not run it a second time.

whatItFakes: The relief-spending-to-votes link is not run: no engine credits the president's party for the disaster relief a town received when its voters choose. (economy-to-approval is carried by the voting engine's candidateReasons, which reads the national economy.)
why: The relief dollars are recorded (the disasters module pays FEMA public assistance and housing assistance as cash-journal transfers), but the research gives its size in vote share per unit of the log of per-person relief in 2008 dollars, and candidateReasons has no relief term, no per-person relief reading and no way to put today's dollars in 2008 dollars.
replacement: A relief term for the president's party in candidateReasons (src/core2/electorate-inputs.ts), read from the disasters module's recorded payments per person and gated on the town having heard of them, sized from Healy and Malhotra 2009 (Table 5, column 2: .454 points of vote share per unit of ln(1 + relief per person in 2008 dollars)).

whatItFakes: The share of residents receiving SNAP (program.snap-receipt) is a place number in the outcome web's ledger, held at the USDA state level: the SNAP benefit pays households and stops those the work requirement reaches, but no field counts them into the number and no web link moves it.
why: The benefit's recipients are payment obligations in the law-reach store (src/core2/law-reach/group-b-food-aid.ts) and world-metrics counts none of them, so the web has no engine record to read and snap-to-food-insecurity reads a moved part that stays zero.
replacement: A world-metrics field counts the SNAP benefit's recipients by weight and engineMeasures reads it, so the food-insecurity record reads the benefit's own households.

whatItFakes: The share of households that are food insecure (household.food-insecurity) is a place number in the outcome web's ledger: its start is the USDA state level and web links move it; no household's food budget or SNAP receipt decides it. Three links into it are carried by engines instead (links.json carriedBy): the SNAP maximum's and SNAP receipt's by the benefit and the household's monthly purchases (snap-maximum-to-food-insecurity, snap-to-food-insecurity), and the grocery exemption's by the sales tax, the price review and the same purchases (grocery-exemption-to-food-insecurity). What a household cannot buy of its everyday plan, kept on its month as unpaid everyday spending, stands for going without food, with no food line of its own.
why: No engine records a household's food spending against its income or its SNAP benefit; the everyday plan (src/core2/cost-of-living.ts) buys food and other goods from one budget with no food category.
replacement: A food-insecurity record per household from its income, its food prices and its SNAP benefit, counted by weight in world-metrics and read through engineMeasures.

whatItFakes: Reducing occupational licensing (licensing-reform-to-poverty) is meant to open licensed work and raise pay at the bottom, but no engine lets the law change who may take a licensed job, so the law reaches no household's income and the poverty measure does not move for it.
why: The jobs engine has no licensing requirement per occupation to repeal, and the poverty measure is the engine's own count, which the web holds as read, so the link moves nothing.
replacement: The jobs engine reads a licensing law row when seekers match to jobs, so a repeal opens licensed jobs to seekers (pool item world-licensing-reform-jobs).

whatItFakes: Higher graduation is meant to raise adult pay a decade later, but no engine ties schooling to the pay a graduate is hired at, so graduation reaches no household's income and the poverty measure does not move for it.
why: The jobs engine prices a hire from the occupation and market, not from the person's schooling.
replacement: Resolved: the jobs engine prices schooling into every hire (hirePay, schoolingWeekly and schoolingOn in src/core2/modules/jobs.ts reading graduationOf in src/core2/school-outcomes.ts; pool item world-schooling-to-pay), and the poverty count (householdPoverty in src/core2/world-poverty.ts) reads that pay, so graduation-to-poverty is carried by those records (links.json carriedBy), proven by src/core2/jobs-graduation-income.test.ts.

whatItFakes: Five researched links into crime and justice outcomes move nothing, each because the engine that would decide its outcome has no cause, no size or no producer to read. summer-jobs-to-youth-violence: no engine runs a summer jobs program, so no one is a participant, and the 43 percent fall in violent-crime arrests is the participants' own (J-PAL's summary of Heller 2014); the public-safety engine's arrest share-out by age band (arrest in src/core2/public-safety.ts) would read a participant's record once arrests have offenders. graduation-to-incarceration: the research is a person's own drop in the chance of prison (0.76 points for white men, 3.4 for Black men, Lochner and Moretti) with no base chance to make a factor, and no engine decides a person's offense, so the schooling on a person's record (schoolingOn in src/core2/modules/jobs.ts) has nothing to lower (see SG-CORE-crime-offenders and SG-LAW-justice-named-offender-acts). mandatory-minimums-to-incarceration: the state panel study counts mandatory laws and gives no size for one, the question has no starting row and no engine reads it; the court's decision of each counted case (resolveDue in src/core2/public-safety.ts) and a named defendant's custody months (convict in src/core2/modules/justice.ts) would. mandatory-minimum-cut-to-federal-prisoners runs at -0.008, a 0.8 percent fall, which is the anchor's fall in all U.S. prisoners although the link now points at federal prisoners (by the anchor's own arithmetic, about 13,000 fewer of the federal count, the federal fall is about 6 percent, so the size sits on the old base until it is resized); it moves justice.federal-incarcerated-per-100k only in the web's ledger, since no engine sentences or holds federal prisoners and every case is tried in the state's courts. release-lower-level-to-larceny is sized on crime.property (0.0731, the larceny share of the NCVS property total), which the crime engine reads in typeFactor, but no policy question reclassifies low-level offenses, so its cause is never in force. The counted court reads pretrial-detention-to-conviction (resolveDue in src/core2/public-safety.ts), but a named bribery defendant's verdict (hearing and convict in src/core2/modules/justice.ts) is a margin of evidence against the defense, with no rate this proportion can scale, so the named tier does not read it.
why: A link moves an outcome only when the engine that decides it reads the link's cause, from a place's rate or a person's own record, at a size the research gives in that engine's units; for these the cause is unrecorded, the research gives no usable size, or no engine decides the outcome.
replacement: Record each cause (a summer jobs program's participants, a mandatory-minimum floor in a starting law or bill, a low-level-offense reclassification question); give arrests offenders whose own records (schooling, program) an offending engine reads; size each link from its study in the deciding engine's units (the federal cut on the federal count, about -0.06, not the all-prisoner -0.008) and have the engine named above read it; give federal defendants a court engine; give a named defendant's plea a term for custody before trial.
